# Performance check function

```{r performance_check_func}
mod_perf_check <- function(mod_names) {
  for (m in mod_names) {
    
    model <- get(m)
    
    # Diagnostic tests for this model
    diagnostic_summary <- list(
      model = m,
      normality = tryCatch(
        check_normality(model),
        error = function(e) NA
      ),
      heteroscedasticity = tryCatch(
        check_heteroscedasticity(model),
        error = function(e) NA
      ),
      outliers = tryCatch(
        check_outliers(model),
        error = function(e) NA
      )
    )
    
    capture.output(
      print(diagnostic_summary),
      file = paste0("mod_summaries/diagnostics_txt/", m, "_diagnostic_summary.txt")
    )
    
    # Using check_model function
    png(
      paste0("mod_summaries/diagnostics_plots/", m, "_diagnostics.png"),
      width = 1400,
      height = 1000
    )
    print(check_model(model))
    dev.off()
    
    # Typical plots
    png(
      paste0("mod_summaries/diagnostics_plots/", m, "_diagnostics2.png"),
      width = 1400,
      height = 1000
    )
    
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    
    # Residuals vs fitted plot
    plot(
      fitted(model),
      resid(model),
      main = paste0(m, "\nResiduals vs fitted"),
      xlab = "Fitted values",
      ylab = "Residuals",
      pch = 16,
      col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.4)
    )
    abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red")
    
    # Q-Q plot of residuals
    qqnorm(
      resid(model),
      main = paste0(m, "\nNormal Q-Q plot"),
      pch = 16,
      col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.4)
    )
    qqline(resid(model), col = "red", lwd = 2)
    
    dev.off()
  }
}
```


# Data cleaning

## Actigraphy data

Start by selecting relevant variables for the analysis

```{r datcleaning}

# Select relevant columns
part5_allmeas2 <- part5_allmeas %>% 
  dplyr::select(ID,
                filename, 
                calendar_date, 
                weekday, 
                night_number,                   
                dur_day_total_IN_min,           # Total inactivity minutes during day
                dur_day_total_LIG_min,          # Total light activity minutes during day 
                dur_day_total_MOD_min,          # Total moderate activity minutes during day
                dur_day_total_VIG_min,          # Total vigorous activity minutes during day
                sleep_efficiency_after_onset,   # Sleep efficiency
                dur_spt_min,                    # Sleep period (onset-waketime)
                dur_spt_sleep_min,              # Total sleep time (TST)
                daysleeper,                     # Sleep time is during the day (1)/ night (0)
                nonwear_perc_day                # Non-wear percentage during the day
                )
# Add ID and measurement timepoint columns
part5_allmeas2 <- part5_allmeas2 %>%
  mutate(
    ID        = str_extract(ID, "\\d+") %>% as.numeric(),          # e.g. 320
    timepoint = str_extract(filename, "(?<=_)[^_]+")    # e.g. T4
  )
# Check how many timepoints per person
n_summary <- part5_allmeas2 %>%
  dplyr::count(ID, timepoint, name = "n_meas") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_totmeas    = sum(n_meas),
    n_timepoints = dplyr::n(),  # number of distinct timepoints for that ID
    meas_by_tp   = paste0(timepoint, "=", n_meas, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
table(n_summary$n_timepoints) %>% 
  kable(
    col.names = c("Number of timepoints", "Number of Participants"),
    caption = "How many participants have data for 1, 2 3 or all timepoints?",
    row.names = FALSE, align = "c", format = "markdown", digits = 3
  )%>%
  kable_styling()
```

These IDs are in the register (of receiving an actiwatch), but not in the GGIR cleaned summary: `r part_TP_register %>% filter(!(.data[["Participant ID"]] %in% part5_allmeas2$ID)) %>% pull(.data[["Participant ID"]]) %>% unique() `

```{r peopl_timepoint}

part5_allmeas2 %>%
  dplyr::distinct(ID, timepoint) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"))) %>%
  dplyr::count(timepoint, name = "n_people", .drop = FALSE) %>% 
  kable(
    caption = "Number of participants per timepoint",
    col.names = c("Timepoint", "Number of participants"),
    row.names = FALSE, align = "c", format = "markdown", digits = 3
  ) %>% kable_styling()

```


GGIR does the following cleaning:

- A night is excluded from the ‘cleaned’ based on having or not having a sleeplog:

  1. If the study proposed a sleep log to the individuals, then nights are excluded for which the sleep log was not used as a guider, i.e., nights with [cleaningcode](https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter10_SleepAnalysis.html#quality-assurance) not equal to 0 or variable sleep log used equals FALSE. 
  
  2. If the study did not propose a sleep log to the individuals, then all nights are removed with cleaningcode higher than 1.

- A day is excluded if the number of valid hours is less than the one given in the input (here < 16 hours).

Save a register of the comparison between the register and data.

```{r datcleaning2}
part_TP_comparison <- left_join(n_summary, part_TP_register, by = join_by("ID" == "Participant ID")) %>%
  mutate(
    same_tp = ifelse(as.numeric(n_timepoints) == `Number of actiwatches`,"yes", "no") 
  )
# Save to have a register
write.csv(part_TP_comparison, "comparison_TP_in_Part5_summary_Emma_register.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Check unusual missing patterns in the data and make them NA if needed.

```{r datacleaning3}
# Check for weird NA patterns 
na_markers <- list(-9999, -999, -99, "NA", "N/A", "na", "null", "NULL", "None", "", " ")
for (marker in na_markers) {
  count <- sum(part5_allmeas2 == marker, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d\n", deparse(marker), count))
} # No changes
```

We filter daysleepers.

```{r daysleepers}
part5_allmeas2 <- part5_allmeas2 %>% filter(daysleeper != 1)
```

If a person has more than seven measurements, we take those will less non-wear percent during day. This is to align to the experiment, as they were told to use the watch for 7 days.

```{r moresevendays}
# sum(is.na(part5_allmeas2$nonwear_perc_day)) #0
part5_allmeasclean <- part5_allmeas2 %>%
  arrange(ID, timepoint, nonwear_perc_day) %>%
  group_by(ID, timepoint) %>%
  slice_head(n = 7) %>%
  ungroup()
```


To be included in the analysis and for reliability, a participant must have at least 3 valid days of actigraphy data [REF]. We filter those that meet this criteria.

```{r threevaliddays}
part5_allmeasclean2 <- part5_allmeasclean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID, timepoint) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 3) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

data.frame(obs = c(nrow(part5_allmeas2),nrow(part5_allmeasclean2),nrow(part5_allmeas2)-nrow(part5_allmeasclean2)), row.names = c('original','cleaned','removed')) %>% kable(
  col.names = "Observations",
  caption = "Observations in the original GGIR output versus the cleaned data"
) %>% kable_styling()
```

Compute variables needed for analysis but not computed in the output.

```{r extravars}
part5_allmeasclean2 <- part5_allmeasclean2 %>% mutate(
  active_dur = dur_day_total_LIG_min +  dur_day_total_MOD_min +  dur_day_total_VIG_min, 
  mvpa_dur =  dur_day_total_MOD_min +  dur_day_total_VIG_min,
  WASO = dur_spt_min - dur_spt_sleep_min
) %>% rename(
  TST = dur_spt_sleep_min,
  SE = sleep_efficiency_after_onset
)
```

Compute mean variables per ID and timepoint.

```{r meanderiveddat}
part5_meanmeas_derived <- part5_allmeasclean2 %>%
  dplyr::select(-filename, -calendar_date, -weekday, -night_number, -daysleeper, -nonwear_perc_day) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID,timepoint) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = T)),
    .groups =  "drop"
  )
```

Filter those IDs with 2 or more timepoints.

```{r meanderiveddat2}
ID_more1TP <- part5_meanmeas_derived %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_timepoints = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  filter(n_timepoints > 1) %>%
  pull(ID)
part5_meanmeas_derived2 <- part5_meanmeas_derived %>%
  filter(ID %in% ID_more1TP) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4")))

#write.csv(part5_meanmeas_derived2, "clean_dat/final_participant_dat_for_analysis.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Number of unique IDs: `r length(unique(part5_meanmeas_derived2$ID))` 

```{r checks_complexity}
# Check how many timepoints per person
n_summary <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  dplyr::count(ID, timepoint, name = "n_meas") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_totmeas    = sum(n_meas),
    n_timepoints = dplyr::n(),  # number of distinct timepoints for that ID
    meas_by_tp   = paste0(timepoint, "=", n_meas, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
table(n_summary$n_timepoints) %>% 
  kable(
    col.names = c("Number of timepoints", "Number of Participants"),
    caption = "How many participants have data for 1, 2 3 or all timepoints?",
    row.names = FALSE, align = "c", format = "markdown", digits = 3
  )%>%
  kable_styling()
```

**Note:** Due to limited repeated observations per participant and incomplete timepoint coverage, models including random slopes for timepoint won't be estimable. Therefore, random intercept models are used.

## Other data

Take out metadata from sav data frame.

```{r othercleaning}
part_data_other_clean <- part_data_other %>%
  # Remove columns not used
  select(-childethnic_text, -childethnic) %>%
  # Remove metadata
  mutate(
    across(everything(), zap_labels), 
    across(everything(), zap_label),
    across(everything(), zap_formats)
  ) %>%
  # To tibble
  as_tibble()
```

Check for weird NA patterns and make them NA.

```{r othercleaning2}
na_markers <- list("-999.00", -999, -99, "NA", "N/A", "na", "null", "NULL", "None", "", " ")
for (marker in na_markers) {
  count <- sum(part_data_other_clean == marker, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d\n", deparse(marker), count))
}
part_data_other_clean2 <- part_data_other_clean %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace(., . == "", NA))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace(., . == "-999.00", NA))) %>%
  mutate(Age = as.numeric(Age))
```

Reshape data to long version.

```{r otherlong}
part_data_long <- part_data_other_clean2 %>%
  # Remove unused columns
  dplyr::select(-contains("PROMIS")) %>%
  mutate(
    ARCSMean10_pt1 = ARCS10itemMean_pt1
  ) %>%
  # Rename columns with ARCS to same format
  rename(
    # 15 items analysis
    ARCSMean15_pt1 = ARCS10itemMean_pt1,
    ARCSMean15_pt2 = ARCS15itemMean_pt2,
    ARCSMean15_pt3 = ARCS15itemMean_pt3,
    ARCSMean15_pt4 = ARCS15itemMean_pt4,
    # 10 items analysis
    ARCSMean10_pt2 = arcs10_mean_pt2,
    ARCSMean10_pt3 = arcs10_mean_pt3,
    ARCSMean10_pt4 = arcs10_mean_pt4,
  ) %>%
  # Create ID column with numbers only
  mutate(
    ExternalReference = sub("^P002$", "P2", ExternalReference), # Correct error in labelling participant ID
    ID = str_extract(ExternalReference, "\\d+") %>% as.numeric()
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ {
        if (is.character(.x)) {
          x <- .x[!is.na(.x) & .x != ""]
        } else {
          x <- .x[!is.na(.x)]
        }
        if (length(x) == 0) NA else x[1]
      }
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Put columns ending in timepoint in a unique column, and create
  # a timepoint column for each value
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("_(ct|pt)[1-4]"),
    names_to = "name",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    tp = str_extract(name, "(ct|pt)[1-4]"),
    timepoint = recode(
      tp,
      ct1 = "T1", pt1 = "T1",
      ct2 = "T2", pt2 = "T2",
      ct3 = "T3", pt3 = "T3",
      ct4 = "T4", pt4 = "T4"
    ),
    variable = name %>%
      str_remove("_(ct|pt)[1-4]") %>%
      str_replace("__", "_") %>%
      str_remove("_$")
  ) %>%
  select(ID, ExternalReference, Age, childsex, timepoint, variable, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = variable,
    values_from = value
  ) %>%
  arrange(ID, timepoint)

# Make timepoint ordered
part_data_long <- part_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"))
  )
```

Filter IDs that are in the PA and sleep data.

```{r otherfilter}
part_data_long <- part_data_long %>% filter(ID %in% part5_meanmeas_derived2$ID) 
```

# Sleep analysis

We visually inspect trends in the sleep behaviour of the participants over time. 

```{r generalsleep}
# General sleep plot
sleep_plot_df <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, timepoint, WASO, TST, SE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(WASO, TST, SE),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  )

p_sleep <- ggplot(sleep_plot_df, aes(x = timepoint, y = value, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 1, colour = "blue") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1.2, colour = "navy") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2, colour = "navy") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1, colour = "navy") +
  facet_wrap(
    ~metric,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      WASO = "Wake after sleep onset (WASO)",
      TST = "Total sleep time (TST)",
      SE = "Sleep efficiency (SE)"
    ))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sleep over time",
    x = "Timepoint",
    y = "Observed value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
p_sleep
ggsave(p_sleep,filename = "plots_out/generalsleep.png", width = 10, height = 6)
```

A summary of the sleep variables per timepoint can also be obtained. 

```{r sleep_sum}
sleep_desc <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, timepoint, WASO, TST, SE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(WASO, TST, SE),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(metric, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n_distinct(ID),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sleep_desc %>% kable(
  caption = "Summary of sleep variables",
  col.names = c("Metric", "Timepoint", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Median")
) %>% kable_styling()
```

Linear mixed-effects models can be used to examine whether sleep outcomes changed over time. Separate models are fitted for WASO, TST, and SE.

**WASO**

```{r sleep_timetest_waso}
# Raw outcome
waso_time.mod <- lmer(WASO ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(waso_time.mod) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(waso_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?

# Sensitivity check
waso_time.mod2 <- lmer(log(WASO) ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(waso_time.mod2) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(waso_time.mod2, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?

mod_names <- c("waso_time.mod", "waso_time.mod2")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r sleep_timetest_waso_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(24, 44, 60, 66), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(log(WASO) ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

**TST**

```{r sleep_timetest_tst}
tst_time.mod  <- lmer(TST  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(tst_time.mod) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(tst_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?

mod_names <- c("tst_time.mod")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

```{r sleep_timetest_tst_sens, eval = FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Sensitivity check
tst_time.mod2  <- lmer(log(TST)  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(tst_time.mod2) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(tst_time.mod2, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?
mod_names <- c("tst_time.mod2")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r sleep_timetest_tst_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(44, 66), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(TST  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

**SE**

```{r sleep_timetest_se}
se_time.mod   <- lmer(SE ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(se_time.mod) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(se_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?

mod_names <- c("se_time.mod")
mod_perf_check(mod_names)
```

```{r sleep_timetest_se_sens, eval = FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Sensitivity check
se_time.mod2  <- lmer(qlogis(SE)  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(se_time.mod2) # Is there any effect of timepoint?
emmeans(se_time.mod2, pairwise ~ timepoint) # Which timepoints differ from each other?
mod_names <- c("se_time.mod2")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r sleep_timetest_se_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(24, 44, 60, 66), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(SE  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

*Note:* Initial models indicated some violations of model assumptions across sleep parameters. WASO showed substantial positive skewness and heteroscedasticity, with increasing variance at higher values; therefore, WASO was log-transformed prior to analysis. The transformed model demonstrated improved homogeneity of variance and more acceptable residual behaviour, although formal tests of normality remained significant, likely due to sample size. TST and SE exhibited moderate skewness and some evidence of heteroscedasticity; however, these patterns were relatively mild and consistent with the distributions of the variables (e.g., bounded nature of sleep efficiency and occasional short sleep duration). Possible transformations of these variables were explored, but they worsened the results. For the original models, diagnostic plots indicated that residual deviations were not severe, so both outcomes were analysed on the original scale. 
Across all models, a small number of potentially influential observations were identified based on Cook’s distance. These corresponded to extreme but plausible sleep values and were consistent across outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluding these cases yielded comparable results, with no meaningful changes in the direction, magnitude, or statistical significance of effects. Accordingly, all observations were retained.
There was no evidence of a significant effect of timepoint on any of the sleep parameters (WASO, TST, or SE), and pairwise comparisons between timepoints were not statistically significant.

# Physical activity analysis

Physical activity trajectory plot

```{r generalPA}
pa_plot_df <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, timepoint, active_dur, mvpa_dur, dur_day_total_IN_min) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(active_dur, mvpa_dur, dur_day_total_IN_min),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  )
p_pa <- ggplot(pa_plot_df, aes(x = timepoint, y = value, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 1, colour = "blue") +
  stat_summary(
    aes(group = 1),
    fun = mean,
    geom = "line",
    linewidth = 1.2,
```

A summary of the sleep variables per timepoint can be obtained. 

```{r pa_sum}
pa_desc <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, timepoint, active_dur, mvpa_dur, dur_day_total_IN_min) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(active_dur, mvpa_dur, dur_day_total_IN_min),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(metric, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n_distinct(ID),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE) %>% round(2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pa_desc %>% kable(
  caption = "Summary of PA variables",
  col.names = c("Metric", "Timepoint", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Median")
) %>% kable_styling()
```

Linear mixed-effects models can be used to examine whether sleep outcomes changed over time. Separate models are fitted for activity duration, MVPA, inactivity duration, with timepoint as a fixed effect and participant ID as a random intercept.

**Active duration**

```{r pa_timetest_active}
active_time.mod <- lmer(active_dur ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)

anova(active_time.mod) 
emmeans(active_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint)

mod_names <- c("active_time.mod")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r pa_timetest_active_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(159, 169), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(active_dur  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

**MVPA**

```{r pa_timetest_mvpa}
mvpa_time.mod  <- lmer(mvpa_dur  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(mvpa_time.mod) 
emmeans(mvpa_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint)

mod_names <- c("mvpa_time.mod")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r pa_timetest_mvpa_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(74, 128, 151, 175), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(mvpa_dur  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

**Inactive duration**

```{r pa_timetest_inactive}
inact_time.mod   <- lmer(dur_day_total_IN_min   ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = part5_meanmeas_derived2)
anova(inact_time.mod) 
emmeans(inact_time.mod, pairwise ~ timepoint)

mod_names <- c("inact_time.mod")
mod_perf_check(mod_names) 
```

Further outlier checks are carried out: 

```{r pa_timetest_inactive_outliers, results = "hide"}
data_no_out <- part5_meanmeas_derived2[-c(37, 145, 146, 169, 171), ]
mod_log_no_out <- lmer(dur_day_total_IN_min  ~ timepoint + (1 | ID), data = data_no_out)
summary(mod_log_no_out)
```

*Note:* Model diagnostics indicated some heteroscedasticity across outcomes; however, visual inspection of residual plots suggested that these deviations were relatively mild and did not substantially impact model fit or inference. Sensitivity analyses excluding influential observations yielded comparable results, and all observations were retained. There was a significant effect of timepoint on all outcomes. Total daily inactivity was significantly lower at T2 and T3 compared to baseline (T1), while the reduction at T4 did not remain statistically significant after adjustment. Pairwise comparisons indicated no significant differences between follow-up timepoints. In contrast, MVPA and total active time were significantly higher at all follow-up timepoints compared to baseline (all p ≤ .001), with no significant differences observed between T2, T3, and T4. Overall, these findings indicate a consistent pattern of reduced inactivity and increased physical activity from baseline, with improvements largely maintained across follow-up assessments.

**Improvement by T2**

Check improving physical activity, that is, someone improves if the second timepoint available for that person is higher (MVPA, active duration) or lower (inactivity) than the first timepoint available.

```{r PAimprovement}
improve_df <- part5_meanmeas_derived2 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(dur_day_total_IN_min, active_dur, mvpa_dur),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(ID, metric) %>%
  arrange(timepoint, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    improved = case_when(
      first(metric) == "dur_day_total_IN_min" ~ nth(value, 2) < nth(value, 1),
      TRUE ~ nth(value, 2) > nth(value, 1)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_impr <- ggplot(improve_df, aes(x = metric, fill = improved)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Change status",
    values = c("TRUE" = "forestgreen", "FALSE" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Improved", "FALSE" = "Did not improve")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    dur_day_total_IN_min = "Inactivity",
    active_dur = "Active duration",
    mvpa_dur = "MVPA duration"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of participants who improved by metric",
    x = "Metric",
    y = "Number of participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_impr
ggsave(p_impr,filename = "plots_out/meanPAimprovement.png", width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r PAimprovement_table}
improve_table_wide_pct <- improve_df %>%
  mutate(
    change_status = if_else(improved, "Improved", "Did not improve"),
    metric_label = recode(
      metric,
      dur_day_total_IN_min = "Inactivity",
      active_dur = "Active duration",
      mvpa_dur = "MVPA duration"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(metric_label, change_status, name = "n_people") %>%
  group_by(metric_label) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = round(100 * n_people / sum(n_people), 1),
    value = paste0(n_people, " (", percent, "%)")
  ) %>%
  select(metric_label, change_status, value) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = change_status,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = "0 (0%)"
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

improve_table_wide_pct %>% kable(
  caption = "Improving physical activity",
  col.names = c("Measurement", "Did not improve", "Improved")
) %>% kable_styling()
```

## Table of results

```{r sleeppa_restable}
# waso_tab <- tidy(wasoact.mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
#   mutate(outcome = "WASO")

waso_tab <- tidy(wasoact.mod2, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = "WASO",
    estimate = exp(estimate),
    conf.low = exp(conf.low),
    conf.high = exp(conf.high)
  )

tst_tab <- tidy(tstact.mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "TST")
se_tab <- tidy(seact.mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "SE")
model_results <- bind_rows(waso_tab, tst_tab, se_tab)
model_results_clean <- model_results %>%
  select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )

# model_results_clean <- model_results %>%
#   mutate(
#     term = recode(
#       term,
#       `(Intercept)` = "Intercept",
#       mvpa_dur = "MVPA duration",
#       dur_day_total_IN_min = "Inactive duration",
#       dur_day_total_LIG_min = "Light activity duration",
#       timepointT2 = "Timepoint: T2",
#       timepointT3 = "Timepoint: T3",
#       timepointT4 = "Timepoint: T4"
#     ),
#     result = paste0(
#       round(estimate, 3),
#       " [",
#       round(conf.low, 3),
#       ", ",
#       round(conf.high, 3),
#       "], p = ",
#       format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
#     )
#   ) %>%
#   select(outcome, term, result)

model_results_clean <- model_results %>%
  mutate(
    term = recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Intercept",
      mvpa_dur = "MVPA duration",
      dur_day_total_IN_min = "Inactive duration",
      dur_day_total_LIG_min = "Light activity duration",
      timepointT2 = "Timepoint: T2",
      timepointT3 = "Timepoint: T3",
      timepointT4 = "Timepoint: T4"
    ),
    result = case_when(
      outcome == "WASO" ~ paste0(
        round((estimate - 1) * 100, 1), "% [",
        round((conf.low - 1) * 100, 1), ", ",
        round((conf.high - 1) * 100, 1), "], p = ",
        format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
      ),
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        round(estimate, 3),
        " [",
        round(conf.low, 3),
        ", ",
        round(conf.high, 3),
        "], p = ",
        format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(outcome, term, result)


model_results_clean <- model_results_clean %>%
  filter(term != "Intercept")


model_results_wide <- model_results_clean %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = outcome,
    values_from = result
  )


model_results_wide %>% kable(
  caption = "Linear mixed-effects models predicting sleep outcomes from physical activity variables.", 
  col.names = c("Term", "WASO", "TST", "SE")
  ) %>% kable_styling() %>%
   add_footnote("Note. WASO coefficients are presented as percentage change due to log transformation; other outcomes are unstandardised coefficients. Each model included a random intercept for participant ID. T1 was the reference timepoint. CI = 95% confidence interval.", notation="alphabet")
write.csv(model_results_wide, "mod_summaries/pa_sleep_tableresults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Table of results

```{r results_tableH4}
# waso_sleep_tab <- tidy(wasoother.mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  # mutate(outcome = "WASO")

waso_sleep_tab <- tidy(wasoother.mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = "WASO",
    estimate = exp(estimate),
    conf.low = exp(conf.low),
    conf.high = exp(conf.high)
  )

tst_sleep_tab <- tidy(
  tstother.mod,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.method = "Wald"
) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "TST")

se_sleep_tab <- tidy(
  seother.mod,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.method = "Wald"
) %>%
  mutate(outcome = "SE")

sleep_symptom_results <- bind_rows(
  waso_sleep_tab,
  tst_sleep_tab,
  se_sleep_tab
) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    term = recode(
      term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Intercept",
      avpain = "Average pain",
      Depression_Tscore = "Depressive symptoms",
      Anxiety_Tscore = "Anxiety symptoms",
      timepointT2 = "Timepoint: T2",
      timepointT3 = "Timepoint: T3",
      timepointT4 = "Timepoint: T4"
    ),
    result = case_when(
      outcome == "WASO" ~ paste0(
        round((estimate - 1) * 100, 1), "% [",
        round((conf.low - 1) * 100, 1), ", ",
        round((conf.high - 1) * 100, 1), "], p = ",
        format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
      ),
      TRUE ~ paste0(
        round(estimate, 3),
        " [",
        round(conf.low, 3),
        ", ",
        round(conf.high, 3),
        "], p = ",
        format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(term, outcome, result) %>%
  filter(term != "Intercept") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = outcome,
    values_from = result
  )

sleep_symptom_results %>% kable(
  caption = "Linear mixed-effects models predicting sleep outcomes from pain, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms.", 
  col.names = c("Term", "WASO", "TST", "SE")
  ) %>% kable_styling() %>%
   add_footnote("Note. WASO coefficients are presented as percentage change due to log transformation; other outcomes are unstandardised coefficients. Each model included a random intercept for participant ID. T1 was the reference timepoint. CI = confidence interval.", notation="alphabet")
write.csv(sleep_symptom_results, "mod_summaries/sleepothervars_tableresults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# PA and sleep sensitivity analysis

## Individual PA variables and sleep 

```{r sens_sleepandpa}
# WASO
waso_inact.mod <- lmer(log(WASO) ~ dur_day_total_IN_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
waso_lig.mod   <- lmer(log(WASO) ~ dur_day_total_LIG_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
waso_mvpa.mod  <- lmer(log(WASO) ~ mvpa_dur + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)

#TST
tst_inact.mod <- lmer(TST ~ dur_day_total_IN_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
tst_lig.mod   <- lmer(TST ~ dur_day_total_LIG_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
tst_mvpa.mod  <- lmer(TST ~ mvpa_dur + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)

#SE
se_inact.mod <- lmer(SE ~ dur_day_total_IN_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
se_lig.mod   <- lmer(SE ~ dur_day_total_LIG_min + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)
se_mvpa.mod  <- lmer(SE ~ mvpa_dur + timepoint + (1 | ID), data = full_dat)

extract_single_pa <- function(model, outcome, predictor_label, predictor_term) {
  tidy(model, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE, conf.method = "Wald") %>%
    filter(term == predictor_term) %>%
    mutate(
      outcome = outcome,
      predictor = predictor_label,
      # exponentiate only for WASO
      estimate_adj = case_when(
        outcome == "WASO" ~ (exp(estimate) - 1) * 100,
        TRUE ~ estimate
      ),
      conf.low_adj = case_when(
        outcome == "WASO" ~ (exp(conf.low) - 1) * 100,
        TRUE ~ conf.low
      ),
      conf.high_adj = case_when(
        outcome == "WASO" ~ (exp(conf.high) - 1) * 100,
        TRUE ~ conf.high
      ),

      result = case_when(
        outcome == "WASO" ~ paste0(
          round(estimate_adj, 1), "% [",
          round(conf.low_adj, 1), ", ",
          round(conf.high_adj, 1), "], p = ",
          format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
        ),
        outcome == "SE" ~ paste0(
          round(estimate_adj, 4),
          " [",
          round(conf.low_adj, 4),
          ", ",
          round(conf.high_adj, 4),
          "], p = ",
          format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
        ),
        TRUE ~ paste0(
          round(estimate_adj, 2),
          " [",
          round(conf.low_adj, 2),
          ", ",
          round(conf.high_adj, 2),
          "], p = ",
          format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    select(predictor, outcome, result)
}


single_pa_sleep_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_single_pa(waso_inact.mod, "WASO", "Inactive duration", "dur_day_total_IN_min"),
  extract_single_pa(waso_lig.mod,   "WASO", "Light activity duration", "dur_day_total_LIG_min"),
  extract_single_pa(waso_mvpa.mod,  "WASO", "MVPA duration", "mvpa_dur"),
  
  extract_single_pa(tst_inact.mod, "TST", "Inactive duration", "dur_day_total_IN_min"),
  extract_single_pa(tst_lig.mod,   "TST", "Light activity duration", "dur_day_total_LIG_min"),
  extract_single_pa(tst_mvpa.mod,  "TST", "MVPA duration", "mvpa_dur"),
  
  extract_single_pa(se_inact.mod, "SE", "Inactive duration", "dur_day_total_IN_min"),
  extract_single_pa(se_lig.mod,   "SE", "Light activity duration", "dur_day_total_LIG_min"),
  extract_single_pa(se_mvpa.mod,  "SE", "MVPA duration", "mvpa_dur")
) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = outcome,
    values_from = result
  )

single_pa_sleep_results %>% kable(
  caption = "Single-predictor sensitivity models examining associations between physical activity variables and sleep outcomes."
) %>% kable_styling() %>% add_footnote("Each cell reports the unstandardised coefficient for the physical activity predictor from a separate linear mixed-effects model adjusted for timepoint, with a random intercept for participant ID. Values are presented as b [95% CI], p. WASO coefficients are expressed as percentage change due to log transformation. Confidence intervals were estimated using the Wald method.", notation="alphabet")
```
